prose: Security startup Strix reports that one of its AI agents, reading PostHog's source code, found a flaw that let an attacker take over a PostHog account with a single survey link. PostHog had added an optional intro screen to surveys; its description was stored through the API and rendered as raw HTML by the browser SDK on the public hosted survey page.

Because only a report-only content security policy protected the page, an attacker could run JavaScript in a signed-in victim's session. In the test, opening the link was enough to mint a personal API key with maximum scope, and the survey still looked normal. PostHog fixed it quickly and audited all surveys, confirming no exploitation beyond Strix's own tests.
highlights: Stored script in a survey intro description ran in the victim's session
Opening the link was enough to mint a full-scope API key
Page only had a report-only content security policy
Found by a Strix agent during a source review
PostHog fixed it fast and found no exploitation beyond the tests
Dated 28 September 2026, on Hacker News on 7 October
